question.text: The Binomial Option Pricing Model was developed by:

answer.text: Fischer Black and Myron Scholes in 1973

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook attributes the Binomial Option Pricing Model to William Sharpe in 1978. The model represents price evolution as a binomial tree where the underlying can move up or down at each step, and it can be applied to both European and American style options. The Trap: Fischer Black and Myron Scholes published their analytical model in 1973, and Black's variant for futures options appeared in 1976; these are different models from the binomial framework attributed in the workbook to Sharpe. Note: Workbook reference — p.76 (William Sharpe 1978 as developer of the binomial model; model works for European and American options).
